summary: Quarterly renewal check-in. Customer is interested in expanding from hosted to Dedicated (2x reserved capacity), adding EU region, and extending contract by 12 months. Discussed pricing delta, SLA, SOC2 and VPC/on-prem options, and next steps for benchmarking and procurement.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-02 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Eli Shah (Redwood SE), Jared Miles (Lumina VP Eng), Priya Kapoor (Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Procurement)

Auto-generated Summary: Quarterly renewal + expansion conversation; customer leaning toward Dedicated to meet latency SLAs; asks about EU region pricing and SOC2 docs; wants a benchmark run before final PO.

00:00 Jared: ok thanks everyone for making time, uh this is Jared from Lumina, we've got Priya and Carlos on, quick intro from our side then we can hand it off
00:18 Maya: thanks Jared yeah appreciate it, Maya Chen from Redwood, joined by Eli our solutions eng, we're running through renewal and expansion options today, figure out capacity needs and next steps
00:35 Priya: hey all, Priya here, head of ML, we've seen good perf with Redwood hosted but hitting P95 spikes during peak clinical hours and we'd like to discuss dedicated options and also EU region for our EU clinics
00:50 Eli: gotcha, yeah we saw the telemetry you shared, a couple of quick clarifying q's — are the P95 spikes mostly inference latency or queuing during high concurrency?
01:05 Priya: yeah mostly queuing, like the api returns fine but queue times jump, and sometimes we see kv cache warmup issues after short bursts, there's also a couple of regulatory teams asking about data residency so EU region is a hard ask
01:25 Maya: makes sense, and timeline for renewal? you mentioned end of Nov in the email — is that still target?
01:33 Jared: correct, target end-Nov for signing extension, we can do 12 months extra if pricing/commitments look good, but procurement timeline depends on PO paperwork
01:45 Carlos: yes from procurement i'd need an updated quote and PO terms, also confirmation on SOC2 scope and whether EU data stays in EU instances, and any KMS/HSM details
02:02 Eli: quick note — Dedicated will give you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput which should remove those queuing spikes; we can also pin a model variant and enable autoscale burst for short peaks, that was part of the ask iirc
02:22 Priya: okay, what's the expected delta in cost for 2x capacity vs our current hosted run-rate? rough numbers fine
02:32 Maya: ballpark — depends on model family and token volume but for your current usage 2x dedicated pool is roughly 1.6x the hosted monthly spend but with much more predictable latency; we'll include exact numbers in the updated proposal
02:50 Jared: and EU region add-on, is that an extra flat fee or separate capacity pool?
03:00 Eli: EU can be configured either as an additional dedicated pool (recommended for strict residency) or we can route to EU-hosted instances; dedicated EU pool means separate reservation and pricing; we'll include both options in the quote
03:18 Carlos: important for legal — does the EU pool come with separate audit logs and is the control plane customer-managed for private deployments?
03:30 Maya: for Redwood Private/VPC we offer a private control plane option and audit logs; for dedicated in our hosted offering we provide tenant-isolated logs and SOC2 reports, we can also integrate your KMS for key separation
03:48 Priya: cool, on performance—Eli can you outline the benchmark plan? we want to see P50/P95/P99 and token throughput for typical clinical workflows
04:00 Eli: yes, plan is to run a 24-48 hour steady-state with synthetic traffic matching your concurrency plus a series of burst tests to validate autoscale and KV-cache warmup; we'll produce lat/throughput graphs and raw logs; we'll need a small sample of realistic prompts and expected output sizes
04:20 Priya: i can send 3 workloads — triage summarization, patient Q&A, and batch extraction — with expected median lengths
04:30 Eli: perfect, also note we'll test with your model pins and quantization settings you prefer; we'll capture memory/kb cache stats too
04:42 Jared: another question on SLA — for Dedicated do you provide a different uptime SLA and incident response? we had a couple of incidents last quarter on the hosted plan during regional outages
04:55 Maya: Dedicated has higher-backed SLA and a named support contact for enterprise tiers; plus automatic cross-region fallback policy can be configured, though if you require strict EU residency, fallback out of region would be limited by policy
05:10 Carlos: on fallback — we need compliance details. if an EU zone has an outage, do we get async replication to another EU zone or do you fall back to US?
05:24 Eli: by default we replicate data within region; cross-region fallback to non-EU is opt-in and requires controls, we can set up failover to a secondary EU region, depending on capacity availability
05:38 Priya: sounds ok. pricing-wise, if we commit to 12 months and 2x capacity, any discount tiers?
05:45 Maya: yes standard commit discounts apply; for annual reserved capacity we can offer a tiered discount and commit credits, we'll put the exact % in the proposal. there's also an option to prepay to get additional discount
05:58 Jared: procurement ask — can you include the PO language and terms we need to route for legal? Carlos will review
06:08 Carlos: yes please include standard SOW and terms, and if you have a template for EU data processing addendum that helps expedite legal review
06:18 Maya: will do. we'll attach SOC2 report and DPA template to the proposal too.
06:25 Priya: one more tech nit — we saw some model-compat warnings in the logs referencing kv-cache mismatch after quantized model switch, any notes?
06:36 Eli: yeah that's an artifact of mixed-model rollouts; the runtime ensures KV compatibility where possible but when switching quantization profiles there can be cache misses until warmup; our recommend is staged canary rollouts with pre-warming of KV to avoid tail latency hits
06:52 Priya: ok that approach sounds reasonable, we'll want a runbook to coordinate rollouts with our infra team
07:02 Eli: we'll draft a rollout runbook and include recommended pre-warm windows and observability queries
07:14 Jared: timeline recap — we want updated proposal by early next week, run benchmarks mid-Nov, procurement sign off by end-Nov if numbers align; is that workable?
07:28 Maya: yes that's fine. so action items: i'll send proposal with EU and dedicated options, Eli will send benchmark plan and we'll schedule the run, Priya will share workloads, Carlos will send PO timeline
07:40 Carlos: yep i'll aim to have procurement timeline by 11/10, but might be earlier if legal gets the DPA quickly
07:50 Maya: any other open concerns?
07:55 Priya: maybe one ask — can we get a short cost model showing cost per 1k requests at different concurrency levels? helps justify to finance
08:05 Maya: yes we can add a cost-per-1k request table and a sensitivity chart for concurrency vs unit cost
08:15 Jared: ok awesome that's helpful.
08:20 Eli: small note on EU region provisioning lead time — if you want EU dedicated pool, provisioning typical lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity availability, so to hit end-Nov we should lock in by mid-Nov
08:36 Priya: noted, i'll try to prioritize the workloads this week
08:42 Maya: great; last thing — do you prefer follow-up as email with attached proposal or should we block a quick call to walk through numbers?
08:50 Carlos: email works, but maybe one short follow-up call after you send the proposal to answer questions — 30 min max
08:58 Maya: ok we'll send proposal and set a 30 min review slot. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and next steps.
09:06 Jared: thanks all. bye

End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: Some transcription errors present (product names sometimes 'KV cache' appears as 'K Vcache' in raw logs), speaker turns occasionally merged. Intent and action items are captured.
